blocks.x: Blockchain & Digital Trust applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Energy & Utilities, blockchain & digital trust delivers distributed-ledger programs where a shared, verifiable record has economic value: enterprise dlt networks for multi-party workflows, asset tokenization, smart contract engineering and audit, provenance and traceability, decentralized identity with verifiable credentials, and on-chain analytics for compliance. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: enterprise dlt network engineering, asset tokenization & digital assets, smart contract engineering & audit — delivered on Dataq Ledger and Dataq Sentinel with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Guarantees-of-origin and renewable certificates reconcile across registries with fraud exposure; buyers demand verifiable provenance.
Renewable supply and flexible demand make legacy forecasting blind; imbalance costs and curtailment climb while forecasts run on yesterday's methods.
IT/OT convergence, remote access growth and legacy SCADA estates create attack paths with physical consequences; CIP/NIS2 duties expand faster than programs mature.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 6 services from the Blockchain & Digital Trust tower — Enterprise DLT Network Engineering, Asset Tokenization & Digital Assets, Smart Contract Engineering & Audit, Provenance, Traceability & Supply Chain Trust as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: NERC CIP (North America) obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Permissioned networks for multi-party truth: governance, consensus and integration done institutionally.
Instruments as tokens: issuance, custody and lifecycle under securities-law discipline.
Contracts as production software: specification, formal verification and audit before value moves.
Proof, not paperwork: EUDR, DPP and chain-of-custody systems regulators and customers can verify.
Certificate issuance/transfer anchored with registry integration (fraud and double-counting exposure down)
Shared settlement records between generators and offtakers (reconciliation disputes collapse)
Unplanned outage hours on critical assets

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: NERC CIP (North America) and IEC 62443 / 61850. Industrial cybersecurity and substation automation standards. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
